name: The example
why: 3: (2, 3) inside (5, 4) inside (6, 7). (6, 4) cannot hold (5, 4): the heights are equal.

name: Same width
why: 1: boxes with the same width never nest. If you sorted by width and then by height, both rising, the heights 1, 2, 3 look like a chain of 3. Sort equal widths by height, falling.

name: Same height
why: 1: the heights must be strictly smaller too.

name: No boxes
why: 0: with no boxes there is nothing to nest.

name: One box
why: 1: a single box is a chain of one.

name: Equal boxes
why: 1: a box does not fit inside an equal box.

name: No turning
why: 1: (2, 5) would fit inside (4, 3) only if you turned it, and boxes keep their direction.

name: Ten in a chain
why: 10: every box fits in the next larger one. The input order does not matter.

name: 100,000 boxes
why: The O(n²) table compares every pair: 5 × 10⁹ comparisons here. Sort, then find the longest rising run of heights with binary search (lesson 6): O(n log n).
